phases.notes: (Exists) PackageFile header/entry/block parsing, PackageCatalog, tag-hash lookup. Solforge: PackageCatalog.Index.cs metadata index (package-index-v1/<root hash>.bin beside the data cache; headers for every patch file, tables for current packages, name rows; keyed by file name + length + write time, any change rebuilds; disabled cache = no index), PackageFile I/O split (ReadTables/LoadTables(bytes)), CollectNameRows/ApplyNameRows split, PackageCatalog.Search.cs (FindByClass, FindByType, GetPackageGroup, FindPackagesInGroup, GetPackageEntries). Check: tests/SunriseStudio.Packages.Tests (scratch packages always; --game-root times the warm open: 400+ files must open from the index under 1 s, skipped without -Game). Memory mapping not needed; the index is the profiled answer

phases.title: Block Decompression & Oodle Integration
phases.notes: (Exists) OodleDecoder (oo2core_3_win64.dll from the install, thread-safe pooled buffers), PackageKeys AES-128-GCM, raw blocks; no zlib path. Solforge: PackageCatalog.Parallel.cs (MaximumParallelDecodes bound, default min(cores, 8); ReadOriginalParallel warms a tag's blocks through the serial CopyBlock path on a bounded Parallel.For, capped at half the LRU, then assembles serially; ReadOriginalAsync; ReadOriginalAll bounded multi-tag reads in input order). Check: Packages.Tests compares serial vs parallel/all/async/bound-1 on PackageWriter scratch packages (a 1.6 MB 7-block tag); --game-root compares the 32 largest installed multi-block (Oodle + AES) tags on cold catalogs and prints both timings. Synthetic Oodle round trip not possible (no compressor binding); installed blocks cover the Oodle path

phases.title: Checker Phase: Viewport & Geometry Pipeline Audit
phases.notes: Audit check written: tests/SunriseStudio.ViewportPipeline.Tests/AuditChecks.cs, run by verify.ps1 -Game (prints 'skipped:' and passes without --game or a hardware adapter; WARP never benchmarks). It checks 1,002,528 triangles at 1920x1080 >= 60 FPS (120 frames, one sync), map 80EDC19B (Leviathan) in the viewport, and 50 load/unload cycles with < 96 MiB private-byte growth and < 64 MiB DXGI local video-memory growth after warm-up (video skipped when the adapter has no IDXGIAdapter3). The destination and every cycle re-read the map with WorldLoader and render it with game shaders (PrepareNativeScene + SetNativeScene, asserting UseGameShaders and no NativeError), then Clear. Limits: the million-triangle benchmark is a synthetic flat grid on the geometry path, not a game-shader map; the private-byte bound is about 2 MiB a cycle; one map only; 50 full map loads make the run long. Manual steps: (1) run .\verify.ps1 -Game <install> on a machine with a GPU and record the 'audit' lines; (2) look up the Trostland church and Tower plaza map tags and add them to AuditChecks.DestinationMap (or a list) - not known here; (3) open both destinations in Solforge, check 60+ FPS in the View > Statistics overlay
